E|_L\cong\bigoplus_{i=1}^r\mathcal O_L(a_i),
\]

\[
d=\min\left\{n\in\mathbb Z_{\ge2}:\text{there exists a uniform, non-homogeneous algebraic vector bundle on }\mathbb P^n_{\mathbb C}\text{ of some rank }1\le r<2n\right\},
\]
with the convention \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\).

23	\[
24	g^*E\oplus\mathcal O^{R-r}
25	 \cong E\oplus\mathcal O^{R-r}.
26	\]

36	## 2. An explicit rank-nine bundle on \(\mathbb P^5\)

38	Let \(V=\mathbb C^6\), with basis \(e_0,\ldots,e_5\), and regard \(\mathbb P(V)\) as parametrizing one-dimensional subspaces. Write
39	\[
40	0\longrightarrow\mathcal O(-1)
41	 \longrightarrow V\otimes\mathcal O
42	 \longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow0
43	\]
44	for the tautological sequence. Set
45	\[
46	F=\bigwedge\nolimits^2Q.
47	\]
48	It has rank \(10\).
49	
50	Choose the nondegenerate bivector
51	\[
52	w=e_0\wedge e_1+e_2\wedge e_3+e_4\wedge e_5.
53	\]
54	It induces a section \(s_w\) of \(F\).
55	
56	At \(x=[\ell]\), its value is the image of \(w\) in \(\bigwedge^2(V/\ell)\). This image cannot vanish: otherwise \(w\in\ell\wedge V\), which would force \(w\) to have rank at most \(2\), whereas its rank is \(6\).
57	
58	Thus \(s_w\) is nowhere zero, and
59	\[
60	0\longrightarrow\mathcal O
61	 \xrightarrow{s_w}F
62	 \xrightarrow{q_w}E_w
63	 \longrightarrow0                                      \tag{1}
64	\]
65	defines an algebraic vector bundle of rank \(9<2\cdot5\).
66	
67	## 3. Uniformity
68	
69	A projective line \(L\subset\mathbb P(V)\) is \(\mathbb P(U)\) for a two-dimensional subspace \(U\subset V\). On it,
70	\[
71	Q|_L\cong\mathcal O_L(1)\oplus\mathcal O_L^4,
72	\]
73	so
74	\[
75	F|_L\cong\mathcal O_L(1)^4\oplus\mathcal O_L^6.            \tag{2}
76	\]
77	
78	The component of \(s_w|_L\) in the trivial summand is precisely
79	\[
80	\bar w\in\bigwedge\nolimits^2(V/U).
81	\]
82	This component is nonzero. Indeed, if it vanished, then
83	\[
84	w\in U\wedge V.
85	\]
86	Writing \(U=\langle u,v\rangle\), every element of \(U\wedge V\) has the form
87	\[
88	u\wedge a+v\wedge b,
89	\]
90	and hence has rank at most \(4\). Again this contradicts \(\operatorname{rank}(w)=6\).
91	
92	A section of the bundle in (2) whose trivial component is a nonzero constant can be transformed by a bundle automorphism into one of the standard sections of \(\mathcal O_L^6\): first change basis in the trivial summand, then subtract its positive-degree component. Taking the quotient gives
93	\[
94	E_w|_L\cong\mathcal O_L(1)^4\oplus\mathcal O_L^5
95	\]
96	for **every** line \(L\). Thus \(E_w\) is uniform.
97	
98	## 4. Recovering the bivector from the bundle

100	We next prove
101	\[
102	E_w\cong E_{w'}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
103	\mathbb Cw=\mathbb Cw'                                  \tag{3}
104	\]

106	
107	### 4.1. Two vanishings
108	
109	We have
110	\[
111	F^*=\Omega_{\mathbb P^5}^2(2),
112	\]
113	and
114	\[
115	H^0(F^*)=H^1(F^*)=0.                                   \tag{4}
116	\]
117	
118	For completeness, these particular vanishings follow directly from the exterior Euler complex
119	\[
120	0\longrightarrow\Omega^2(2)
121	 \longrightarrow\bigwedge\nolimits^2V^*\otimes\mathcal O
122	 \longrightarrow V^*\otimes\mathcal O(1)
123	 \longrightarrow\mathcal O(2)\longrightarrow0.
124	\]
125	Its complex of global sections is
126	\[
127	0\longrightarrow\bigwedge\nolimits^2V^*
128	 \longrightarrow V^*\otimes V^*
129	 \longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}^2V^*
130	 \longrightarrow0,
131	\]
132	which is exact. The other terms have no positive-degree cohomology.
133	
134	### 4.2. Simplicity of \(F\)
135	
136	We also need
137	\[
138	\operatorname{End}(F)=\mathbb C.                         \tag{5}
139	\]
140	
141	The exterior tautological resolution gives
142	\[
143	H^0(F)=\bigwedge\nolimits^2V.
144	\]
145	An endomorphism of \(F\) consequently induces a linear map \(A\) on \(\bigwedge^2V\) preserving, for every nonzero \(x\in V\), the evaluation kernel
146	\[
147	x\wedge V.
148	\]
149	For independent \(x,y\),
150	\[
151	(x\wedge V)\cap(y\wedge V)=\mathbb C(x\wedge y).
152	\]
153	Therefore every decomposable bivector is an eigenvector of \(A\).
154	
155	In particular, write
156	\[
157	A(e_i\wedge e_j)=\lambda_{ij}e_i\wedge e_j.
158	\]
159	Applying the same observation to \((e_i+e_k)\wedge e_j\) shows
160	\(\lambda_{ij}=\lambda_{kj}\) whenever \(i,j,k\) are distinct. All the eigenvalues are equal, so \(A\) is scalar. Since \(F\) is globally generated, its original endomorphism is scalar as well. This proves (5).
161	
162	### 4.3. Uniqueness of the quotient map
163	
164	Apply \(\operatorname{Hom}(F,-)\) to (1). Equations (4) and (5) imply
165	\[
166	\operatorname{Hom}(F,E_w)\cong\mathbb C,
167	\]
168	generated by \(q_w\).
169	
170	If \(\phi:E_w\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}E_{w'}\), then
171	\[
172	\phi q_w=cq_{w'}
173	\]
174	for some nonzero scalar \(c\). Their kernels in \(F\) coincide. Hence the two nowhere-zero sections defining these kernels differ by a nonzero constant, proving (3).
175	
176	## 5. Non-homogeneity
177	
178	The natural projective-linear action on \(F\) carries the construction for \(w\) to that for the corresponding transformed bivector.
179	
180	Take the projective automorphism induced by
181	\[
182	g=\operatorname{diag}(2,1,1,1,1,1).
183	\]
184	Its action sends \(w\) to
185	\[
186	2e_0\wedge e_1+e_2\wedge e_3+e_4\wedge e_5,
187	\]
188	which is not proportional to \(w\). The inverse action likewise gives a nonproportional bivector, so the choice of pullback convention is immaterial.
189	
190	By (3), the corresponding pullback of \(E_w\) is not isomorphic to \(E_w\). Thus \(E_w\) is **not homogeneous**.
191	
192	This proves \(d\leq5\), completing the mathematical argument.
193	
194	## 6. Executable symbolic checks
195	
196	Here is Python using only SymPy. It checks the linear algebra underlying the construction, the global-section exactness used in (4), the eigenvalue constraints used in (5), and the explicit transformation used to disprove homogeneity.
197	
198	It also independently computes the Chern character from the resolution
199	\[
200	0\longrightarrow\mathcal O(-2)
201	 \longrightarrow V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)
202	 \longrightarrow
203	 \bigl(\bigwedge\nolimits^2V/\mathbb Cw\bigr)\otimes\mathcal O
204	 \longrightarrow E_w\longrightarrow0.
205	\]
206	
207	```python
208	import sympy as s
209	from itertools import combinations, permutations
210	
211	N = 6
212	pairs = list(combinations(range(N), 2))
213	
214	# The chosen nondegenerate bivector.
215	W = s.zeros(N)
216	for i in range(0, N, 2):
217	    W[i, i + 1] = 1
218	    W[i + 1, i] = -1
219	assert W.rank() == 6
220	
221	# Representatives of the two symplectic types of two-plane:
222	# non-isotropic and isotropic. Their projected bivectors are nonzero.
223	for U, expected_rank in [([0, 1], 4), ([0, 2], 2)]:
224	    rest = [i for i in range(N) if i not in U]
225	    assert W.extract(rest, rest).rank() == expected_rank
226	
227	# Universal factorization:
228	# u wedge a + v wedge b = M J M^t, with M having only four columns.
229	# Therefore every bivector in <u,v> wedge V has rank at most four.
230	u, v, a, b = [
231	    s.Matrix(s.symbols(f"{name}0:6"))
232	    for name in ["u", "v", "a", "b"]
233	]
234	M = s.Matrix.hstack(u, v, a, b)
235	J = s.zeros(4)
236	J[0, 2] = J[1, 3] = 1
237	J[2, 0] = J[3, 1] = -1
238	assert M * J * M.T == (
239	    u*a.T - a*u.T + v*b.T - b*v.T
240	)
241	
242	# Simplicity: all 15 eigenvalues lambda_ij must coincide.
243	# Check that the displayed equality constraints have rank 14.
244	rows = []
245	for i, j, k in permutations(range(N), 3):
246	    row = [0] * len(pairs)
247	    row[pairs.index(tuple(sorted((i, j))))] = 1
248	    row[pairs.index(tuple(sorted((k, j))))] -= 1
249	    rows.append(row)
250	assert s.Matrix(rows).rank() == 14
251	
252	# Degree-two Koszul exactness:
253	# wedge^2 V* -> V* tensor V* -> Sym^2 V*.
254	monomials = sorted(pairs + [(i, i) for i in range(N)])
255	mult = s.zeros(len(monomials), N*N)
256	alt = s.zeros(N*N, len(pairs))
257	
258	for i in range(N):
259	    for j in range(N):
260	        mult[monomials.index(tuple(sorted((i, j)))), N*i+j] = 1
261	
262	for col, (i, j) in enumerate(pairs):
263	    alt[N*i+j, col] = 1
264	    alt[N*j+i, col] = -1
265	
266	assert mult.rank() == 21
267	assert alt.rank() == 15
268	assert mult * alt == s.zeros(21, 15)
269	assert 36 - mult.rank() == alt.rank()
270	
271	# The explicit automorphism changes the projective bivector.
272	g = s.diag(2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1)
273	Wp = g * W * g.T
274	assert s.Matrix.hstack(
275	    W.reshape(36, 1), Wp.reshape(36, 1)
276	).rank() == 2
277	
278	# Independent Chern-character and Chern-class checks.
279	h = s.symbols("h")
280	ch = s.series(
281	    14 - 6*s.exp(-h) + s.exp(-2*h), h, 0, 6
282	).removeO()
283	
284	log_c = sum(
285	    (-1)**(k-1) * s.factorial(k-1) * ch.coeff(h, k) * h**k
286	    for k in range(1, 6)
287	)
288	c = s.series(s.exp(log_c), h, 0, 6).removeO().expand()
289	
290	assert ch.coeff(h, 0) == 9
291	assert c == 1 + 4*h + 9*h**2 + 14*h**3 + 14*h**4
292	
293	print("All assertions passed.")
294	print("ch(E) =", ch)
295	print("c(E)  =", c)
296	```
